intake.domain: open-set intent detection with known-only boundary calibration
intake.compute: existing frozen-MiniLM caches and bounded CPU/GPU pilot budget
intake.expertise: open-set recognition, sentence representations, reproducible evaluation
intake.baseline: fixed single/multi-centroid MiniLM Gate, MOGB, ADB, DA-ADB, DCLOOS
intake.limitation: current fixed multi-centroid Gate can improve one dataset while expanding the union of accepted regions and causing false acceptance on another; current calibration evidence does not support a legal universal K or lambda selector

bottleneck_statement: The current line of work can fit class centers and per-center radii, but it has no protocol-level quantity that measures the incremental open-space risk created when several accepted regions are unioned: a configuration can preserve or improve Known coverage while accepting a disproportionate amount of unknown space, and the failure is dataset-dependent rather than exposed by center stability alone. This is visible in arxiv:2607.07974v1, whose multi-cluster MiniLM claim does not establish stability or protection against boundary-union false acceptance, and is consistent with arxiv:2602.21252v1, which treats context-conditioned boundaries as necessary because a static boundary can mismatch the operating condition but does not supply a known-only selector for semantic OOS risk. The missing quantity is a legally estimable, test-independent estimate of the extra rejection risk of a multi-region gate, not another unvalidated K or lambda sweep.

closest_adjacent.summary_and_residue: The paper replaces a single MiniLM boundary with fixed multi-cluster boundaries for OOS intent detection and reports gains across three datasets. Its abstract does not establish a test-independent estimate of the incremental open-space risk of the union of local regions, and the anchor full text remained unfetchable after top-up [residue is abstract-level: anchor fulltext unfetchable].

INTACT conditions an anomaly boundary on declared intent and policy context in a different security domain. It does not close the semantic OOS problem of selecting whether an additional local region is safe when no validation unknown-intent labels are available.

InverseNet isolates operator mismatch and calibration confounds in cross-modal benchmark comparisons. It diagnoses mismatch but does not produce a per-intent, known-only risk estimate for the acceptance union of semantic intent boundaries.

what_phase_0_did_not_address: No retrieved leaf estimates, with a held-out and test-independent protocol, how much additional unknown-space acceptance is caused by adding a second or later region to a known intent.

No retrieved leaf tests whether the shared assumption that per-region distance/radius scores are sufficient for open-set acceptance remains valid when the final decision is an arbitrary union of regions.
No retrieved leaf gives a legal selection rule that can retain K=1 for unsafe intents and allow extra regions only when Known coverage and open-space risk are jointly acceptable across datasets.

method_lineage.line: known-only open-set intent recognition from class representation to multi-region boundary acceptance

nodes.move: root formulation predicts one of the observed intent classes
nodes.residual_problem: unknown intents are forced into a known class

nodes.move: adds an acceptance region around known representations and rejects points outside it
nodes.residual_problem: one region may not describe heterogeneous known intent geometry and threshold choice can trade false rejection against false acceptance

nodes.move: learns a more flexible representation or boundary from known data instead of a fixed distance geometry
nodes.residual_problem: flexibility can improve coverage but does not by itself quantify the open-space risk of multiple accepted regions

nodes.move: replaces one region with multiple local regions in a lightweight sentence-embedding space
nodes.residual_problem: the union can over-accept unknown space and no legal selector is established for when extra regions are safe

nodes.move: conditions the boundary on intent or policy context rather than using one static rule
nodes.residual_problem: the cross-domain result does not specify known-only semantic OOS risk control for multi-region unions

nodes.move: holds hidden operator and evaluation factors fixed to expose mismatch
nodes.residual_problem: the diagnostic does not yield an operating selector for multi-region open-set risk

method_lineage.notes: Retrieved nodes are citable; parametric ancestry is awareness-only. The current paper is the anchor frontier leaf. Collateral nodes are not gap sites.

domain_pattern_distribution.notes: Assumption auditing, controlled diagnostics, and conditioning are the most frequent families, but no single family is saturated; their shared residue is the lack of a legal semantic open-space risk selector.
